briefdescription.para: Base for configuration sections that read typed values from the process environment.

detaileddescription.para: This header defines EnvLoader, a reusable base class that turns raw environment strings into the specific types the server uses: integers, strings, booleans, durations (lengths of time) and sets of comma-separated names. Each conversion has a fallback default so a missing or badly written variable never stops the server from starting; problems are logged instead. Configuration sections inherit from this class and call its helpers.

WHY THIS FILE MATTERS IN THE SERVER: Every section of Configurator (server, database, DoS limits, tokens, and so on) derives from EnvLoader, so this is the shared engine behind all configuration loading. It is the middle layer: EnvVars below it reads the raw text, and the Configurator sections above it call getEnvironmentVariable() to obtain ready-to-use typed values. Without it, each section would have to duplicate parsing and error handling, and a single malformed variable could crash startup.

CONCEPTS TO LEARN (for beginners):
Environment variables: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/environ.7.html
Function templates: https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/function_template
std::chrono durations (lengths of time): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/chrono/duration
std::unordered_set (a collection of unique values): https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/container/unordered_set
